### 2026-10-23 – I worked on the firmware for PocketSynth. Initially I wrote a very simple script that used the arduino tone() function to generate a note for each key pressed. However to better resemble a real instru

**2.93h**

I worked on the firmware for PocketSynth. Initially I wrote a very simple script that used the arduino tone() function to generate a note for each key pressed. However to better resemble a real instrument, I rewrote the firmware to instead allow for multiple keys to be played at once, allowing for proper chords and more diverse music. I may add on to this in the future, however for the time being after doing some research as to how to properly generate constructive notes, I believe the code should work as intended.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/363b57a6-3349-4b4b-9c9e-9a726d55176a/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-25 – I decided I wanted to add a way to change the octave of the synthesizer. So I redisigned the PCB and enclosure to accomodate an additional button and modified the firmware to cycle between 3 differenc

**2.5h**

I decided I wanted to add a way to change the octave of the synthesizer. So I redisigned the PCB and enclosure to accomodate an additional button and modified the firmware to cycle between 3 difference octaves. I also chose to switch the keys to actual key switches for a more interactive feel, and thus modified the PCB and enclosure accordingly
